metaTitle: Sliding Glass Door Repair Fort Lauderdale | Salt and Rollers
description: Sliding glass door repair in Fort Lauderdale near canals and the beach: why salt kills rollers first, a yearly care schedule, and condo permit rules.
h1: Sliding glass door repair in Fort Lauderdale
subline: With 165 miles of inland waterways in the city, salt air reaches a lot of sliders, and the rollers and lock usually feel it first.
answer: Sliding glass door repair in Fort Lauderdale is mostly a salt problem. Near canals, the Intracoastal and the beach, salt corrodes rollers and locks first, so doors grind, skid and stop latching. Stainless rollers hold up better near the water. Condo owners replacing a door need the association and a city permit.
faqHeading: Questions about salt, tides and doors in Fort Lauderdale
closing: If your door grinds or won't latch, send a photo of the track and the bottom corners of the panel, or give us a call.

faqs.q: Do king tides affect sliding glass doors in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: Only if salt water reaches the door. The city says its highest tides typically come in September, October and November, and low streets and yards can flood. If tide water got onto your patio, rinse the track with fresh water that week so salt doesn't sit under the rollers.

faqs.q: Can a Fort Lauderdale condo owner skip the door permit under the new HB 803 exemption?
faqs.a: No. The city's HB 803 guide lists condominium, multifamily and apartment properties as not exempt, along with window replacements and properties in a flood hazard area. The exemption took effect July 1, 2026 and needs written approval even where it applies.

faqs.q: Why do the rollers on my canal-front slider rust when the door never gets rained on?
faqs.a: Salt air is enough. It settles in the sill and draws moisture, and a steel roller in an aluminum panel corrodes faster with salt around it. That's why we lean toward stainless rollers on doors within sight of the water, when the right size exists.

faqs.q: When is the best time of year to service a slider in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: April or May, before hurricane season starts on June 1. Test the lock, check that the panel closes flush and clear the weep holes. On a waterfront door, a quick track cleaning every month and a closer look every three months keep salt from building up.

faqs.q: Can a salt-stiffened lock on a Fort Lauderdale slider be cleaned instead of replaced?
faqs.a: Often, if the corrosion is on the outside. Cleaning, a lubricant the door maker approves and an adjustment can bring a stiff latch back. If the lock body is corroded inside or the latch hook is pitted, replacing the lock is the fix that lasts.
